patient does not like meat. Eats ﬁ sh,

Usual dietary intake:
• Drinks 64 ounces of caffeinated

milk, or water.
• Rarely drinks alcohol, nonsmoker. 
Eats one time per day in the early

Evaluation of Assessment Data
A thorough nutritional analysis and
examination of repeated laboratory 
values is essential. The caloric content
of the diet is marginal and the protein
content is low. The non-heme iron in
the patient’s diet is poorly absorbed,
and there may be additional interfer-
ence with mineral absorption due to
higher ﬁ ber intake, as ﬁ ber may bind
trace elements. Supplementation does
